clue.text: Opening of Clapham Junction after a container crane incident ultimately leads to gathering at Number Ten?

indicators.note: the junction word is placed after everything before it in the clue
the opening of a word is its first letter, so Clapham gives only its initial

parts.note: first letter of Clapham
a bin is a container

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of each of crane and incident

parts.note: last letter of crane
last letter of incident
a junction is a meeting point, so meeting

explanation.surface: A news report: a crane accident at a busy London railway station prompts an emergency session in Downing Street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clapham Junction' reads as the famous London station, but the two words do separate jobs: 'Junction' is the meeting point that comes last in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Number Ten Downing Street is the Prime Minister's residence, where senior ministers assemble; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: I value what bank offers

parts.note: I is the symbol for electrical current in physics
account means value or importance, as in of no account

explanation.surface: A customer says they appreciate the services of their bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' looks like the speaker but is the physics symbol for current.
explanation.definitionFit: A current account is the everyday banking product for deposits and payments, which banks provide to customers.

clue.text: Hair cutting ceremony with, say, knight shaving it

parts.note: a bris is the Jewish circumcision ceremony

indicators.note: shaving means trimming off, so the letters of it are removed

parts.note: a knighthood is an example of a title
taken as written

explanation.surface: A haircut at a ceremony where a knight is having a shave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hair cutting' looks like one phrase, but 'Hair' is the definition and 'cutting ceremony' is BRIS. TITLE loses IT to leave TLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A bristle is a short stiff hair, as on a brush or a pig's back.

clue.text: Reportedly understands truce is something that can protect bridge

indicators.note: reportedly means as people say it, so the words are taken as heard

parts.note: knows means understands and peace is a truce

explanation.surface: A news item claims someone grasps the terms of an armistice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridge' suggests a river crossing or the card game, but it is the bridge of the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosepiece is the part of a helmet or spectacles guarding the bridge of the nose.

clue.text: Dope mostly affected way of speaking

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: twee means affected or precious
RP is Received Pronunciation, the standard British accent

explanation.surface: Someone's accent is largely put on.
explanation.walkthrough: RP, Received Pronunciation, is the prestige accent of British English.
explanation.definitionFit: A dope is a fool, and a twerp is a silly or annoying person.

clue.text: See 1
It gives speaker a boost having name included in redesigned home page

indicators.note: included in means put inside, so the name letter goes into the rearranged letters
redesigned means reworked, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: A web designer revamps a website's front page, adding a name to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A megaphone is a cone that amplifies the voice of whoever talks into it.

clue.text: Cancel Caesarean section on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection shows things the wrong way round, so the letters run backwards
a section is a part, so the letters are a run inside the word

parts.note: letters three to seven of Caesarean

explanation.surface: A surgeon decides, after thinking it over, to call off a planned operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caesarean section' is one medical phrase in the surface, but 'section' takes a part of 'Caesarean'.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase is to wipe out or delete, which is to cancel.

clue.text: Press release primarily covers old English heavy metal producer?

parts.note: to iron clothes is to press them

indicators.note: covers here means sits over, so the release letter is set among the old English letters
primarily picks the first letter

parts.note: first letter of release

explanation.surface: A press statement about a heavy metal band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heavy metal' suggests rock music; iron ore yields iron, a heavy metal, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron ore is rock mined and smelted to obtain iron.

clue.text: Trouble I got with car park after scratching front of hatchback arriving at transport hub

indicators.note: trouble means disturb, so the letters are rearranged
scratching means striking out, so a letter is taken from the pool before rearranging
front of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of hatchback

explanation.surface: A motorist has trouble parking at the airport and scratches the front of a hatchback.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove H (front of hatchback) from I GOT WITH CAR PARK and rearrange the remaining letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Gatwick is London's second-largest airport, a major hub for travel.

clue.text: New edition's more detailed about wanting feminine energy

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the letters run backwards
wanting means lacking, so the feminine letter goes and the energy letter takes its place

parts.note: fussier means more elaborate or more detailed
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A publisher notes that the new edition is more thorough than the old one.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the F of FUSSIER for E to get EUSSIER, then 'about' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A reissue is a fresh printing or release of something already published.

clue.text: Change course of attack on Indian State

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece being on another means it comes after it

parts.note: Goa is a state on India's west coast
a bout is an attack or fit, as in a bout of flu

explanation.surface: A military report of an assault on a region of India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change course of attack' looks like one phrase; the definition ends at 'course' and 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In sailing, to go about is to tack, turning the vessel onto a new heading.

clue.text: Drink of Cognac, say — maintaining temperature — with soft finish

indicators.note: maintaining means holding, so the temperature letter is held inside the drink

parts.note: eau is French for water, a drink in Cognac, a French town
p (piano) is the musical marking for soft

explanation.surface: Advice on how to serve a brandy: at the right temperature, with a smooth aftertaste.
explanation.walkthrough: Cognac is the town, not the brandy: the drink of a French place is French water, EAU.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat up is to finish one's food completely, so the phrase means finish.

clue.text: Sausages provided energy before exercise class with cycling club

indicators.note: the energy and exercise pieces come before the club

parts.note: pep is energy or vigour
PE is physical education, a school exercise class

indicators.note: cycling moves a letter round from the front of the word to its back

parts.note: an iron is a golf club

explanation.surface: A fitness note: sausages gave one the energy for a gym class, done with a cycling club.
explanation.walkthrough: IRON has its first letter sent to the back by 'cycling', giving RONI.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepperoni is a spicy Italian-American cured sausage, and the word is often used for slices of it.

clue.text: Other tune's composed in addition

indicators.note: composed here means arranged, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A musician has written a different melody.
explanation.definitionFit: Thereunto is an old formal word meaning besides or moreover, added to that.

clue.text: Reorder hot drink with mug as accessory

indicators.note: reorder means put in a different sequence, so the pieces are rearranged

parts.note: to neck is British slang for drinking quickly
a mug is a fool, as is a clot

explanation.surface: Order another hot drink with a mug as an extra.
explanation.walkthrough: The three pieces H, NECK and CLOT are put in a new order; 'neck' is British slang for drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A neckcloth is a cravat or scarf worn around the neck, an item of dress added to an outfit.

clue.text: Dictator's investment cut

indicators.note: a dictator here is one who dictates, speaking words aloud, so the word is as heard

parts.note: a stake is a share invested in a business

explanation.surface: A tyrant's financial holding has been reduced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dictator' suggests a tyrant, but it is someone dictating, which signals a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A steak is a cut of meat, a thick slice from a carcass.

clue.text: Important motorsport's boring round of competition

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so the motorsport letters go inside

parts.note: seminal means highly influential or important
F1 is Formula One, written with I for 1

explanation.surface: A judgement that a major racing series is dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' reads as dull but means drilling into; F1 enters as FI.
explanation.definitionFit: A semi-final is the penultimate stage of a knockout tournament.

clue.text: To some extent Asda is leading supermarket sector

indicators.note: To some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Asda, a British supermarket chain, is partly ahead in the retail sector.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a passage between shelves, the section of a shop you walk down.

clue.text: See 1
Quiet source for milk shake

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
a cow's udder is where milk comes from

explanation.surface: A calm request for the origin of a milkshake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'milk shake' reads as a drink, but 'shake' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To shudder is to tremble or quiver suddenly.

clue.text: Pretend to consume loads before a drink

indicators.note: the first part comes before the final A
to consume means to take in, so the loads go inside the word for pretend

parts.note: to cod is a British slang verb meaning to pretend or hoax
reams means loads, a great quantity

explanation.surface: Someone fakes eating a lot before having a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cod', British slang for hoax or pretend, surrounds REAMS, then A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Cream soda is a sweet fizzy soft drink flavoured with vanilla.

clue.text: Exaggerate too much on the subject of, say, golf

parts.note: over can mean about, as in a quarrel over money

G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A golfer overstates things when talking about the sport.
explanation.definitionFit: To over-egg is to overdo or overstate something, adding more than needed.

clue.text: See 8
Doctor cures cat and a group of lobsters?

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A vet treats a cat and a few lobsters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link: only CURES CAT and A are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Crustacea is the class of arthropods including lobsters, crabs and shrimps; lobsters are one example, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Sailors discovered hip bones

indicators.note: discovered means with its cover off, so the outer letters go

parts.note: the middle letter of hip

explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered' reads as found, but it means uncovered: hip loses its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarsi are the small bones of the ankle, the plural of tarsus.

clue.text: A court journalist had an effect

parts.note: ed, short for editor, is a journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter covering a trial made a difference.
explanation.definitionFit: Acted means took effect or worked, as a drug acted quickly.

clue.text: French poet's always bolder

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A French poet is forever more daring.
explanation.definitionFit: Freer means less restrained or more uninhibited, behaving more boldly.

clue.text: Open to take in some work experience

indicators.note: to take in means to hold inside, so the work unit goes within the word for open

parts.note: to undo a knot or parcel is to open it
an erg is a small unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: Someone is willing to try a spell of work experience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work experience' looks like one phrase, but 'some work' is the physics unit ERG and 'experience' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To undergo is to go through or be subjected to something, as in undergo surgery.

clue.text: Regularly using train set — fine but not King's Cross

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter, here the first, third and fifth of train

parts.note: alternate letters of train

indicators.note: but not means the king letter is dropped from the word for fine

parts.note: OK means fine, all right
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Using a model railway set, all is fine except at King's Cross, the London station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King's Cross' is split: K is removed from OK to leave O, and 'Cross' is the definition, a hybrid.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangelo is a hybrid fruit bred from tangerine and pomelo, so it is a cross.

clue.text: Ski yoghurt with the lid broken — missing half your sweet

indicators.note: broken means smashed apart, so the letters are rearranged
missing means the letters of half your are not part of the answer once the rest is rearranged
half here keeps the first two of the four letters of your

parts.note: first half of the word your

explanation.surface: A pot of yoghurt with a broken lid has lost half its contents, a mishap at a skiing resort.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of SKI YOGHURT THE LID, remove YO (half of 'your'), and rearrange the rest; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Turkish delight is a gel confection dusted with sugar, a classic sweet.
